headline: Referred non-citizen voting and amended ModernGov charter changes to City Council, recommending both go on the ballot.
summary: Before voting, the committee heard support for non-citizen voting. On ModernGov, the proposal would set three-year terms for mayoral appointees and move four positions to career administrator jobs, and several members wanted the HR and Planning Director posts kept as mayoral appointments.
decisions: Referred the non-citizen voting charter change to City Council with a recommendation to adopt the resolution to put it on the ballot, unanimously.
Referred the ModernGov charter change to City Council as amended by the committee, with a recommendation to adopt the resolution to place it on the ballot, unanimously.

Page 1 of 4 
 
 
Charter Change Committee 
 Thursday, November 19, 2026 
Remote via Zoom/In-Person in Front Conference Room, 645 Pine St, Burlington, Vermont 
DRAFT MINUTES 
  
Members Present:  Becca Brown McKnight (Chair), Gene Bergman, Buddy Singh, Marek 
Broderick 
  
Staff Present: Jessica Brown (City Attorney), Katherine Schad (Chief Administrative Officer), 
Lisa Gerlach (Chief of Staff) 
 
Public Present: Sarah Carpenter (City Councilor), Allie Schachter (City Councilor) 
 
Meeting called to order at 12:04 PM by Councilor McKnight. 
  
1.   Adopt the Agenda 
     1.01 Adopt the Agenda 
  
Motion to Adopt Agenda as written.  
 
Motion by Councilor Singh, Seconded by Councilor Bergman 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
2.   Adopt the Minutes 
     2.01 Motion to adopt draft minutes from October 15, 2026 
  
Motion to adopt the draft minutes from October 15, 2026 as written.   
 
Motion by Councilor Bergman, Seconded by Councilor Singh 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
3.    Public Forum 
      3.01 Verbal Comments 
 
There were no speakers present.   
 
Public forum closed at 12:05 PM.   
 
4.    Non-Citizen Voting 
      4.01 Non-citizen voting 
 
Councilor Schachter voiced her support and recounted support received from REIB and the 
community.
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
The Committee voiced unanimous support for this charter change.   
 
CAO Schad clarified the Clerk-Treasurer's Office is not releasing citizenship data but that this 
change would legally cement the City’s authority to follow that policy.   
 
Motion to refer the Non-citizen Voting charter change item to City Council with the 
recommendation of adopting the resolution to put the item on the ballot.   
 
Motion by Councilor Bergman, Seconded by Councilor Singh 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
5.  ModernGov 
     5.01 ModernGov discussion 
 
CAO Schad presented to the Committee on the proposed changes captured by the ModernGov 
charter change: 
• Move all mayoral appointments to a three-year term to coincide with the Mayor’s term.  
• Move four positions from appointed to career administrator positions, to include Planning 
Director, HR Director, Assessor, and Chief Information Officer.  
• Non-department head level appointments would be eliminated.  The Zoning 
Administrative Officer was left off the list provided but will be added back in and 
expressed in the motion language to City Council.  
• Organizational restructuring of CEDO and Department of Finance and Administration 
(DFA), where Office of City Planning and Business & Workforce Development will be 
housed under CEDO, and DFA’s departments of CT, Assessor, HR, and I&T will be 
formalized under the leadership of the CAO.  Changes to the Church Street Marketplace 
are not being requested and the CSM Director will still be appointed but operationally 
continues to report to the CEDO Director. 
 
Councilor Bergman asked if the language regarding mayoral appointments should be changed to 
clarify appointments coincide with the commencement of a mayor’s term rather than the election 
of a mayor.  Councilor Bergman also noted that budget resolutions need to include the directive 
that the CSM Director reports to the CEDO Director.  Attorney Brown agreed with Councilor 
Bergman’s points regarding the language and explained the provision of 15 months is to account 
for cases where a mayor appoints someone in their last year and the number aligns with the start 
of a new fiscal year. 
 
Councilor Singh flagged career appointments for CIO makes sense but is concerned about HR 
and Planning because if a new mayor wants to take Planning in a whole new direction, that 
should be the new executive’s prerogative, and understands the proposal stipulates they are at-
will employees but wants to think it over more.  Councilor Singh expressed support for keeping 
CSM separate from CEDO and City Council retaining those appointments.
Page 3 of 4 
 
 
Councilor Broderick voiced support for the three-year appointments but wants the Committee to 
consider the provisions for removal by Council and shares Councilor Singh’s concerns about 
making the HR and Planning Director career positions.   
 
Councilor Carpenter noted she supports the bulk of the proposal and does not take issue with the 
reporting structure but agrees with Councilors Broderick and Singh that HR Director and 
Planning should remain as mayoral appointments so the City Council has more of a chance to vet 
them as well.  Councilor Carpenter also asked if the Church Street Marketplace Commission had 
a chance to weigh in on the proposal.   
 
Councilor Schachter echoed previous councilors’ concerns about Planning and HR Directors and 
wants to know the pros and cons of keeping the mayoral appointments versus career positions.  
Councilor Schachter also noted that CEDO has diverse workstreams, such as homelessness 
response and Church Street Marketplace initiatives, and worries about the sustainability of 
keeping them housed under one department, pointing out that formalizing changes in the charter 
may not be the best approach if we do not have enough information to know that this structure 
has been working.   
 
Councilor Brown McKnight stated to move it forward, she would like to see the Planning and 
HR Director changes removed as well as clarifying the Church Street Marketplace changes, and 
questions if the restructuring changes regarding CEDO need to be added to the charter.   
 
CAO Schad noted Councilor Singh’s preference that the Church Street Marketplace Director 
report to the Mayor.   
 
Chief of Staff Gerlach advised the Administration’s thought process was to distinguish between 
Department Heads and Directors, by setting Department Heads as mayoral appointments and 
Directors as civil servant positions, and is receptive to the Committee’s amendments to the 
proposal to keep it moving forward to the Council.   
 
Councilor Carpenter asked staff about making the proposed language broader in regards to the 
organizational changes.  Attorney Brown clarified the thinking was that as CT, Assessor, IT, and 
HR are established in the charter, then in order to merge them under a new department, that new 
department must also be established in the charter and asked for the Committee’s 
counterproposal if formalizing those changes in charter is not desired.  Chief Gerlach said she 
would consult with the Mayor for direction if the Committee does not want to put organizational 
changes in the charter.  Councilor Carpenter clarified wanting to maintain future flexibility since 
charter changes are cumbersome, not that she opposes the changes themselves.   
 
Councilor Singh echoed Councilor Carpenter’s point about flexibility for reorganization and 
emphasized it is important for fee-payers of the Church Street Marketplace to maintain their 
voice.   
 
Councilor Bergman stated that the CSM Director would still have access to the Mayor for 
important, non-operational issues and believes that separating the workflows in CEDO into silos 
would be more ineffective than bringing them together and and does not think the proposed
Page 4 of 4 
 
 
language is too prescriptive and would support keeping HR and Planning Directors as mayoral 
appointments so the Committee can reach consensus.  Councilor Bergman also noted there are 
removal mechanisms for appointments and directors, and that if the Committee wanted to take 
up a more comprehensive rewrite of the Charter in terms of structuring departments, he would be 
willing to put in that time.   
 
Motion to refer the proposed ModernGov charter change to City Council as amended by the 
Committee, and recommend adoption of the resolution to place on the ballot.  
 
Motion by Councilor Bergman, Seconded by Councilor Singh 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
 
6.  Adjournment 
     6.01 Motion to adjourn 
 
The next meeting was set for Thursday 12/3 at 5:30. The meeting was adjourned with no 
objection at 1:08 PM.
